about: SUPPORT-1 · built by support/buildIndex.mjs from Steward's own sources. Do not edit by hand.

passages.title: Home
passages.text: Home is your tap on the shoulder each morning: the people who need you today, each with one next step.

passages.title: Home
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
Home opens with today's date and a greeting, and under it a box where you can ask Steward a question about your records, or tell it what to do. Below that are sections, in this order unless you change it: "Set up Steward" (a checklist while you are getting started), The Thread, Drift, monthly gifts that need you, thank-yous ready, Sequences, and "Tell Steward what to do".
The Thread shows "First thing": one person and their next step. Drift lists donors who have gone quiet past their own giving pattern. The right rail, "Today", has three tiles: "Open follow-ups", "Due today" and the monthly givers whose card failed this week. Click a tile to see the people behind it.
If you have connected a calendar and have meetings today, a short brief for each one appears at the top.
After a meeting, type what happened and Steward reads your note for a pledge, a gift, a fund and a next step, shown under "Steward heard". Each one quotes your own words, and nothing is recorded until you press save. With AI turned off, a simpler reader does the same job and says so. You can also get these meeting briefs by email each morning: tick "Your meetings today" in Settings, under Account.

passages.title: Home
passages.heading: Work through The Thread
passages.text:
1. Read the person and the step under "First thing".
2. Click "Open" with their name to see their record, or "Mark it done" to log the conversation.
3. If it is not for today, click "Not today" and choose "No longer a prospect", "Handled outside Steward" or a date to revisit, then "Snooze".
4. Click "Show them" to see everyone coming up this week, and "Done" on any row to log it.

passages.title: Home
passages.heading: Change the layout
passages.text:
1. Click "Edit" at the top right.
2. Drag a section to move it, or use "↑ Top" to send it to the top.
3. Click "Hide" on a section you do not want. Hidden sections wait in a tray, each with "Show".
4. Click "Done" to save, "Cancel" to discard, or "Reset to default".

passages.title: Home
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: The layout is yours alone and follows you to another browser. The Thread and "Tell Steward what to do" are always shown. Typing in "Tell Steward what to do" and pressing "Go" opens Agent with your words; nothing runs until you confirm a plan there.

passages.title: Tasks
passages.text: Tasks is your list of follow-ups and next steps, sorted by the day they are due.

passages.title: Tasks
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
The screen is titled "Your tasks." At the top is a box where you add a task in plain words. Below it are six tabs, each with a count: Today, Upcoming (the next seven days), Overdue, Later (more than seven days away), No date, and Done (finished in the last 30 days).
Each row shows the task, its day, the person it is about (click the name to open their record), and a button for what the task asks for, such as "Log the call", "Draft the email" or "Draft the thank-you". Every open task also has "Snooze".
"Mine" shows the tasks that are yours and "Everyone" shows the whole organization's. An admin can also pick one person's tasks from "Any staff member".

passages.title: Tasks
passages.heading: Add a task
passages.text:
1. Type it in the box at the top in plain words, for example "Call Bill Harmon Friday 2pm about the gala", then click "Add" or press Enter.
2. Steward shows what it read: the task, who it is about, the day, the time and the kind (Call, Email, Meeting, Thank-you, Write or Other). Change anything that is wrong. If more than one person matches the name, choose under "Which one?".
3. Click "Save task". An Undo appears for a moment in case you change your mind.

passages.title: Tasks
passages.heading: Change, finish or snooze a task
passages.text:
1. Click a task to open it. You can change the task, its day and time, kind, priority (Normal or High), its owner and whether it repeats (every week, every month on the same day, every month on the first Monday, or every quarter), and add notes and a checklist. Click "Save".
2. Click the round box beside a task to finish it. For a call or a meeting with a person, Steward asks how it went and what the next step is, then "Save and mark done". Tick "No next step" if there is none.
3. Click "Snooze" to move it to "Tomorrow", "Next week" or a day you pick, with an optional reason that stays on the task.
4. To work on several at once, click "Select" (or press and hold a task on a phone), tick the tasks, then "Reassign", "Move", "Mark done" or "Delete".

passages.title: Tasks
passages.heading: What this screen does not do
passages.text:
Tasks never sends anything by itself. "Draft the email" and "Draft the thank-you" open a draft for you to read, and it goes only when you press send. A task that belongs to something else, like a step in a journey or a grant deadline, is changed where it lives rather than deleted here.
If your subscription has lapsed, you can see your tasks but not add or change them.

passages.title: Calendar
passages.text: Calendar puts everything with a date in one place: meetings, next steps, shifts, events and more.

passages.title: Calendar
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
Week is the first view; Day, Month and Agenda are beside it (on a phone, Agenda comes first, with a strip of days at the top). Meetings, next steps and tasks, volunteer shifts (with how many places are filled), events, journey steps, campaign sends and pledge payments each have their own color and their own tick box on the left. Birthdays are there too, ticked off until you want them.
"Mine" shows what is yours; "Everyone" shows the whole organization. An admin can also pick one person. The line across today is the current time, and the times are your organization's time zone, named under the tick boxes.
A small brass dot means something needs a look: two of your meetings at once, a shift short of people, or an event on top of a shift.

passages.title: Calendar
passages.heading: Move something
passages.text:
1. Drag a meeting, a next step, a shift or an event to a new day or time. Drag the bottom edge of a meeting, shift or event to change how long it is.
2. The change saves straight away, and "Undo" at the bottom of the screen puts it back.
3. A meeting from your Google or Outlook calendar moves there too. If your calendar will not take the change, Steward says so and nothing moves.

passages.title: Calendar
passages.heading: Add something
passages.text:
1. Click an empty slot (on a phone, press +).
2. Choose Meeting, Call, Next step, Shift or Event. The form opens with that day and time filled in; find the person by name where there is one.

passages.title: Calendar
passages.heading: Ask about the dates on screen
passages.text: "What's my week look like?" counts what is on the calendar and points out anything that needs a look. "Who am I meeting this week and when did they last give?" lists each meeting with that person's last gift. The box beside them answers other questions about the same dates.

passages.title: Calendar
passages.heading: What this screen does not do
passages.text: Journey steps, campaign sends, pledge payments and birthdays are moved where they live, not by dragging here. Clicking any of them opens it.

passages.title: Donors
passages.text: Donors is everyone who ever believed in your work, one record each, where you search, filter and open a person's whole story.

passages.title: Donors
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
The screen is titled "Your donors." Along the top are the search box, the views (Directory, Team for admins, Re-engage, Map and Data health), "✦ Call List", "Log a call", "+ Add" and "↑ Import & tools ▾".
The Directory lists each person with their stage, owner, lifetime giving, last gift and giving strength. Use the stage, owner and designation menus to narrow it, or open "⊞ Filters" for more: stage, giving pattern, geography, last gift, lifetime giving and custom fields. Re-engage gathers lapsed donors. Map shows where people live. Data health lists records that need tidying, such as possible duplicates.

passages.title: Donors
passages.heading: Add a donor
passages.text:
1. Click "+ Add". A "New Donor" card opens.
2. Pick a stage, then fill in Full Name, Email and Phone.
3. Click "Save".

passages.title: Donors
passages.heading: Record a gift
passages.text: There is no gift button on the list itself. Open the person, go to "Gifts & pledges" and click "+ Add Gift". The "Gift Amount ($)" box on the new donor card sets their totals only and does not create a dated gift, so record the real gift on their record.

passages.title: Donors
passages.heading: Act on several people at once
passages.text:
1. Click "Select" and tick the rows you want.
2. Choose "Plan a follow-up". You also get "+ Add to pipeline" and "Move to stage ▾", and admins can use "Assign owner ▾" and "Delete". "Delete" takes a donor off your lists and totals; Steward keeps the record, so support can bring it back. To remove a person for good, use Erase on their profile.

passages.title: Donors
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: "Export CSV" exports what the search and the stage, owner and designation menus match. The advanced filters only narrow the page you are looking at, and a badge says so. To bring people in from a file, see Import donors.

passages.title: Groups
passages.text: A group is a list of people with a name, kept by hand or by a rule, that works wherever a list does.

passages.title: Groups
passages.heading: Two kinds
passages.text:
A group kept by hand holds the people you put in it until somebody takes them out. Add people from the Donors list (click "Select", tick them, then "Add to a group") or from a person's profile, under their name.
A group by rule carries a lightning mark. Its rule is the same filters the Donors list has: role, giving level, lifecycle, closeness, whether they have given, and stage. Every rule must hold. Who is in it is worked out fresh each time, so a gift that takes somebody to Mid moves them into a Mid group the moment it is recorded, and a refund that takes them back under moves them out. "Warm volunteers who have never given" is one rule: Volunteers, Warm, Has never given.

passages.title: Groups
passages.heading: Start from a list Steward already sees
passages.text:
1. Open Groups. Under "Start from a list Steward already sees" are starter groups such as "Gave last year, not yet this year", "Monthly givers", "Volunteers who have never given" and "Board members", each with how many of your people fit it today.
2. Click one to see who is in it, then "Add". It becomes a group by rule that keeps itself up to date.
3. To make your own, click "New group".

passages.title: Groups
passages.heading: A group's page
passages.text: Each group shows how many people are in it, their average gift, what they gave this fiscal year and in total, how many gifts that is, and the last twelve months month by month. Click any number to see the people or gifts behind it. The list of people can be narrowed to Mid or Major.

passages.title: Groups
passages.heading: Where a group works
passages.text: "Email this group" opens a new campaign for it, and "Start a journey" starts one for it. A group can be the audience of a campaign, a tag in your email tool (Settings, Connections), who a journey is for, what starts a journey ("They join a group"), who a survey goes to, and a filter on a saved dashboard and its board pack, where it narrows the gift figures to the group's people.

passages.title: Journeys
passages.text: A journey is how you look after somebody, written down once, so no new donor slips away unnoticed: it starts on its own and reminds your team one step at a time.

passages.title: Journeys
passages.heading: What a journey is
passages.text:
A journey starts when something happens to a person, such as a first gift, and then puts a step in front of whoever owns the relationship at the right time. It never sends anything. Every step waits for you. If a step has a draft, Steward writes it for you to read, and it is still yours to send.
You can open Journeys from the rail or from Settings, under Journeys. Both show the same builder. Only admins can create or change a journey; everyone else can read them.

passages.title: Journeys
passages.heading: Create a journey
passages.text:
1. Click "Create a journey", or pick one of the cards under "Start from one of these", such as New donor, first year.
2. Fill in "What it is called" and "One line about it".
3. Under "When it starts", choose the trigger, for example "They give for the first time" or "You put them in it yourself".
4. If you want, narrow "Who it is for" by stage, tag or gift size.
5. Click "Create it". The journey starts off, with one step.

passages.title: Journeys
passages.heading: Edit the steps
passages.text:
1. Open the journey and click a step.
2. Set "What happens", "What kind of step", "When" and "Whose step it is".
3. Choose "Draft in your voice" if you want Steward to prepare words for you, and add "A note for whoever does it".
4. Use "Add one after" or "Add a step before" to build it out.
5. Click "Save the journey", then choose who the change applies to.

passages.title: Journeys
passages.heading: Turn it on
passages.text:
1. Click "Turn it on".
2. To include people who already qualify, click "Apply to people who already qualify" and confirm.

passages.title: Communications
passages.text: Communications is where you write and send email campaigns, build sequences and approve milestone emails.

passages.title: Communications
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text: The tabs are Overview, Campaigns, Templates, Audience, Analytics, Sequences, Your email tool, Drafts to review and Surveys. Overview shows how many people you can reach, recent sends and your audiences. A campaign is a Draft, Scheduled, Sending or Sent.

passages.title: Communications
passages.heading: Send a campaign
passages.text:
1. Open Campaigns and click "+ New Campaign". Start from a template with "Use this →" or from blank.
2. Fill in "Campaign Name", "Subject Line" and "Audience Segment".
3. Write the email under "Email Body". "Donation link" adds a link to give. The preview shows what one person will see.
4. Click "Send me a test" to check it in your own inbox.
5. Click "Save draft", or "↑ Send to" the number shown. Confirm the dialog, which reminds you it sends real emails.

passages.title: Communications
passages.heading: Schedule instead
passages.text: Set "Send it later" before you save, and the send button becomes "Schedule". Leave it empty to send it yourself. Only admins see the send and schedule buttons; staff can save drafts for an admin to send.

passages.title: Communications
passages.heading: Sequences
passages.text:
1. Open Sequences and click "New sequence".
2. Fill in "What is it called" and "What starts it", then add steps with "+ Add a step".
3. Click "Save, and leave it off".
4. Click "Preview" to read it, then "Turn on" and "Turn it on" when you are ready. "Turn off" stops it.

passages.title: Communications
passages.heading: Drafts to review
passages.text:
Steward drafts it. You send it. Emails Steward drafts for a giving milestone, an anniversary or a workflow you turned on wait here, and nothing goes to a donor until somebody sends it.
Each draft has "Send", "Mark reviewed", "Edit" and "Dismiss". Saving an edit also marks it reviewed. "Send all reviewed" sends every draft marked reviewed, and only those.

passages.title: Communications
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: Your email tool reports on sends from Mailchimp or Constant Contact once connected. It cannot resend them. "Email this audience" on Audience opens a new campaign; choose who it goes to under "Audience Segment".

passages.title: Donor Portal
passages.text: Donor Portal turns on and shares your branded donor sign-in page. It is shown only to organizations on the Portal plan.

passages.title: Donor Portal
passages.heading: Who sees this
passages.text: Donor Portal is hidden from the navigation for most organizations. Nothing behind it is deleted. If your organization is on the Portal plan, it is your main screen, and Settings has a matching Donor Portal section with an "Open Donor Portal →" button.

passages.title: Donor Portal
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
A card titled "Your donor portal" with a Live or Off marker and three buttons: "Edit the portal", "Open the live portal ↗" and "Copy link". Below it are campaign stories, Impact Updates, and engagement for the last 30 days: sign-ins, dashboard views, impact views and receipt downloads.
The switches and updates are for admins. Other roles see them greyed out.

passages.title: Donor Portal
passages.heading: Turn the portal on
passages.text:
1. Tick the portal switch so it reads on.
2. If you want donors to find you in the directory, tick "List this organization in donor dashboards" and fill in the one-line description, city and state. These save on their own.
3. Click "Copy link" and share it with your donors.
4. Click "Edit the portal" to change how it looks.

passages.title: Donor Portal
passages.heading: Post an impact update
passages.text:
1. Under "Impact Updates", click "+ New update".
2. Add a title, the story and any photos, and choose which donors it shows to.
3. Click "Publish update". It appears in the portal. It is not emailed.

passages.title: Fundraising
passages.text: Fundraising is the place for money coming in: goals, campaigns, pages, auctions, peer-to-peer, recurring gifts, memberships, major gifts and deposits.

passages.title: Fundraising
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
The screen is titled "Your fundraising." with four sections. Overview shows your goals, what you have raised this period, active campaigns, live giving pages and recent gifts. Campaigns & pages holds Campaigns, Giving pages & forms, Tickets & sponsors, Auctions, Peer-to-peer, Recurring and Memberships. Major gifts holds At a glance, Pipeline, Proposals, Portfolios and Plans. Money in holds To confirm, Deposits, Acknowledgments, Funds and Started, not finished.
Auctions, Peer-to-peer and Memberships also have their own entries in the sidebar, under Raise, and each one opens its part of this screen.

passages.title: Fundraising
passages.heading: Create a campaign
passages.text:
1. Open Campaigns & pages, then Campaigns, and click "+ New campaign".
2. Fill in "Campaign name", "Goal amount", "Type", "Start date" and "Deadline".
3. Under "What donors see", add the donor-facing name, a short description, the story and a photo.
4. Tick "Show goal progress to donors" if you want them to see it.
5. Click "Create campaign".

passages.title: Fundraising
passages.heading: Record a deposit
passages.text:
1. Open Money in, then Deposits, and click "Add a deposit".
2. Fill in "Deposit date", "Slip total" and the lines, then click "Read the slip" and check it before you commit.

passages.title: Fundraising
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text:
Start a giving page with "New giving page" under Giving pages & forms. Each page has "Edit in editor", "Open page", "Copy link" and "QR and embed". Nothing changes for donors until you publish.
"Propose a recurring gift" under Recurring emails the donor a proposal. Nothing changes until they accept, and the link lasts 14 days.
When a bank reissues a card, Stripe can update the saved card by itself, and Steward notes it on the donor's timeline and counts it on Recurring under "Cards updated automatically". Whether a card is updated depends on the card network and on your organization's own Stripe account; a card that is not updated still goes to failed-card recovery.
Every plan includes the Pipeline. Moving a card asks what happened.
Proposals are started from a person's record with "+ New proposal". Plans never send anything.
"Mark as sent" under Acknowledgments records the gifts as thanked by letter. It does not send anything.

passages.title: Events
passages.text: Events tracks galas, dinners, site visits and the like: who came, where they sat, and the follow-up.

passages.title: Events
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text: The screen is titled "Your events." with tiles for events this year, total attendees, event revenue and average attendance. Switch between "Upcoming", "Past" and "All". Each event card shows its figures, and you can click them to see the rows behind them.

passages.title: Events
passages.heading: Create an event
passages.text:
1. Click "+ New Event".
2. Fill in "Event Name", "Event Type" and "Date". Add an end date, location, description, capacity and estimated cost if you have them.
3. Click "Create Event →".

passages.title: Events
passages.heading: Add guests
passages.text:
1. Open the event and click "Add Attendees".
2. Choose "From Directory" to pick people already on file, or "Add Guest" to type a name and an optional email.
3. Set each person's status: Invited, Confirmed, Attended, No Show or Cancelled.

passages.title: Events
passages.heading: On the night
passages.text:
1. Under "Tables and seating", click "Add tables", then "Seat everyone". Read the plan and click "Seat them", or "Leave it as it is".
2. Use "Print the chart" and "Print name tags" if you want paper.
3. Under "Check-in", scan a ticket or type a name, then tap the person to check them in. Tap again to undo.

passages.title: Events
passages.heading: Afterwards
passages.text:
Click "✦ Create Follow-up Tasks" to give every attendee a task. "Draft a thank-you per sponsor" puts drafts in Agent for you to review; Steward sends none of them.
Ticket and sponsorship levels are set in Fundraising, under Campaigns & pages, then Events, not here. The event's goal shows "None set" because there is no goal field yet.

passages.title: Grants
passages.text: Grants tracks applications from first research to award, with the deadlines Steward watches for you.

passages.title: Grants
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
Six tabs: Pipeline, Funders, Deadlines, Library, Reports and "✦ Find grants". Pipeline shows every grant as a "Board" with eight stages (Prospecting, LOI, Invited, Submitted, Awarded, Declined, Reporting and Closed), or as a "List". Each card shows the ask, the funder and the next deadline.
Funders keeps one page per funder, Library holds the text and documents you reuse in applications, and Reports shows how the year's grants stand.

passages.title: Grants
passages.heading: Add a grant
passages.text:
1. On Pipeline, click "Add a grant".
2. Fill in "Funder", and if you have them, "Program", "Ask ($)", "Program officer", the stage and a deadline.
3. Click "Save grant". An Undo appears for a moment.

passages.title: Grants
passages.heading: Move a grant along
passages.text:
1. Drag its card to the next stage on the board. On a phone, choose the stage instead.
2. Moving a grant to Declined asks why, so next year's ask can start from it. Undo puts a move back.

passages.title: Grants
passages.heading: Add a deadline
passages.text:
1. Open the grant and click "Add a deadline".
2. Pick the kind: LOI due, Proposal due, Decision expected, Report due, Renewal window opens, or Custom.
3. Pick the date, add a note if you want, and click "Add".
4. When it is handled, click "Done". "Edit" changes it and "Take off" removes it.

passages.title: Grants
passages.heading: Deadlines tab
passages.text: Lists the open deadlines for the next twelve months. When one is near, a follow-up opens for the grant's officer. Admins can change how early that happens under "How early Steward reminds you" and "Save lead times".

passages.title: Grants
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: Deleting a grant asks you to confirm, then removes it for good, with its deadlines and notes. To bring grants in from a file, click "Bring in a spreadsheet" on Pipeline, or use Donors, "↑ Import & tools ▾", "Import grants".

passages.title: Volunteers
passages.text: Volunteers keeps your roster, schedules shifts, checks people in and records their hours and waivers, on the same record as their gifts.

passages.title: Volunteers
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
The screen is titled "Your volunteers." in four sections. People holds the Roster. Schedule holds Opportunities and shifts, Groups and Check-in. Records holds Shifts and hours, Waivers and checks, and the Hours report. Reach holds your Sign-up link. Volunteers are people on file like everyone else, so they share one record and one timeline with their giving.
A volunteer coordinator does not see the giving parts of this screen.

passages.title: Volunteers
passages.heading: Add a volunteer
passages.text:
1. In People, click "Add a volunteer".
2. Fill in their name, email and phone.
3. Click "Add them", then "Add another" or "Done".

passages.title: Volunteers
passages.heading: Set up a shift
passages.text:
1. In Schedule, open Opportunities and shifts and click "New opportunity".
2. Name it, say what it is and where, and tick "Needs a signed waiver" or "Needs a background check" if it does. Click "Create it".
3. On the opportunity, click "Add a shift", set the date, times and how many people, and click "Add it".
4. Click "Copy sign-up link" to share it.

passages.title: Volunteers
passages.heading: Record hours
passages.text:
1. In Records, open Shifts and hours and click "Log a shift".
2. Pick who volunteered, the date, the hours and what they did.
3. Click "Log shift".

passages.title: Volunteers
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: Check-in rounds hours to the nearest quarter hour. "Import volunteers" takes a CSV or Excel file, and "Undo this import" is offered afterwards. "Download for a funder" in the Hours report gives you a file to send.

passages.title: Finance
passages.text: Finance is the ledger: transactions, funds, budgets, payouts, restricted money and the month-end exports.

passages.title: Finance
passages.heading: Who sees this
passages.text: Every plan includes Finance. It starts hidden for volunteer coordinators, who can show it again by customizing their sidebar.

passages.title: Finance
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text: The screen is titled "Your money." with a "Year basis" switch for Fiscal Year or Calendar Year. Overview shows money in by month, what needs you, cash on hand, revenue, expenses and surplus, and your fund balances. Funds holds Funds and Budgets. Deposits and payouts holds Payouts and the Deposit sheet, whose "Open the deposit sheet" button opens the slip right there. Grants money holds Restricted. Exports holds Month close, Year-end statements and the Audit log.

passages.title: Finance
passages.heading: Log a transaction
passages.text:
1. Open Transactions and click "+ Add transaction".
2. Choose "↑ Money in" or "↓ Money out".
3. Fill in the date, amount, description, account and fund.
4. Click "Save transaction".
5. If it looks like a donor's gift, Steward asks whether to "Log as a gift" instead.

passages.title: Finance
passages.heading: Add a fund
passages.text:
1. Open Funds and click "+ Add fund".
2. Give it a name and description, and tick the restricted box if a donor or grant restricted it.
3. Click "Save".

passages.title: Finance
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: Budgets are edited by clicking a cell. In Month close, the download stays greyed out until the month's deposits balance. Year-end statements is a pointer: the run itself is in Settings, under Tax Receipts. To record a bank deposit, use "Open the deposit sheet" here, or Fundraising, Money in, Deposits, "Add a deposit". Both open the same sheet.

passages.title: Reports
passages.text: Reports holds every report and the four dashboards, and lets you build and save your own.

passages.title: Reports
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
The screen is titled "Your Reports". The rail on the left has "Build a report", a search box, and groups: Dashboards (Board, Fundraising, People and Recurring, any dashboards your team saved, "Board pack", "Past reports" and "New dashboard"), Your saved reports, Who stopped giving, Who gives the most, The year, Money in, Grants, and Volunteers and members.
Who stopped giving holds LYBUNT, SYBUNT, lapsed donors and retention. Every figure comes with the sentence that defines it, and clicking a figure shows the rows behind it.

passages.title: Reports
passages.heading: Run and export a report
passages.text:
1. Pick a report in the rail.
2. Click "Download CSV". LYBUNT, SYBUNT, Retention and Top donors also offer "PDF".
3. On a dashboard, click "Export PDF" for a copy to share with your board.

passages.title: Reports
passages.heading: Build your own
passages.text:
1. Click "Build a report".
2. Choose what it is about under "A report about…", then pick "Columns".
3. Add filters with "Add a filter", and group them with "Add a group" if you need to.
4. If you want totals, set "Group and total by". Click "Run it".
5. Type a name in "Name this report". Tick "Share with everyone here" or "Email it to me every Monday" if you want.
6. Click "Save report". It appears under Your saved reports.

passages.title: Reports
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: A saved report cannot be edited or deleted yet; build a new one if you need a change.

passages.title: Agent
passages.text: Agent is where you tell Steward what to do in plain words. It shows you the plan, and nothing happens until you say yes.

passages.title: Agent
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text: Six tabs: Plans, Ask, Workflows, Waiting for you, What changed (what each import and connection read brought in) and Guardrails. Steward reads, counts, finds people and drafts. It never records money on its own, refunds, changes a pledge or a monthly gift, or issues a tax receipt.

passages.title: Agent
passages.heading: What it can do for you
passages.text:
Tell it in your own words and it does the work through the same buttons you would press, as you, and checks each result before it says Done:
People: change an email, phone or address; make a colleague someone's owner; move their stage; add them to or take them out of a group; put them in a household.
Conversations: log a call, meeting or email with its date, which updates last contact everywhere; set or replace their next step with a due date.
Volunteers: make someone a volunteer with hours a week, days and roles; sign them up for a shift; log hours they gave.
Journeys and events: start or stop a journey for one person or a list; put someone on the guest list of a free event.
Gifts: when you tell it a gift arrived, it prepares the gift as one card, and nothing is recorded until you press Record. It can mark a gift thanked.
Duplicates: it proposes that two records are one person, at the top of Data health, and you press Merge.
If part of what you asked is something it cannot do, the plan says so in one sentence at the top instead of leaving a note. If a name matches more than one person, it asks which before it changes anything. A step that ran but whose result is not there says Failed, with the reason, never Done. Everything it does is in the audit log as the Agent, approved by you, with your words as the reason, and can be undone for thirty days.

passages.title: Agent
passages.heading: Ask for something
passages.text:
1. In Plans, type what you want, for example "Draft a thank-you to every donor who gave this month".
2. Click "Show me the plan". Steward lists each step.
3. Read it. Click "Run the plan" to go ahead, or "Not this one" to drop it.
4. A simple question, such as a count, is answered at once, and Steward writes nothing.

passages.title: Agent
passages.heading: Review what is waiting
passages.text:
1. Open "Waiting for you". Items are oldest first.
2. Read each one: a gift to confirm, a thank-you draft, a note.
3. Click "Approve", or "Skip" and say why if you want.

passages.title: Agent
passages.heading: Workflows
passages.text:
Workflows are ready-made recipes you switch on, such as a follow-up when a monthly card fails. Each has "Turn on", its own settings and "View activity".
Steward drafts it. You send it. A recipe never emails a donor. When a recipe writes an email (the first-gift thank-you, the failed-card note, the optional re-engagement email), the draft waits in Communications under Drafts to review until somebody reads it and sends it.

passages.title: Agent
passages.heading: Guardrails
passages.text: Guardrails lists what Steward may and may not do, every instruction you have given, and every change it made, each with "Undo" for thirty days. "Pause everything" stops it at once. Admins can use "Turn drafting off" or "Turn on drafting".

passages.title: Settings
passages.text: Settings is where your organization, team, connections, receipts, data and security are set up.

passages.title: Settings
passages.heading: The sections
passages.text:
Organization: your name, mission, staff and board, and your brand. Team: who can sign in, and invites. Connections: every outside service in one place, from Stripe and PayPal to your inbox, your books and API keys, and whether each one is still working. Giving Pages: your time zone, donor-covers-fees and your giving pages. Customization: custom fields and impact metrics. Your words: what you call donors and gifts. Journeys. Tax Receipts. Brand kit: your logo, colors and fonts for emails and pages. Imports. Audit log (admins). Privacy: privacy mode for people you serve. Your Data. Account. Security.
Organizations on the Portal plan also see a Donor Portal section.

passages.title: Settings
passages.heading: Find a setting
passages.text:
1. Click Settings at the bottom of the sidebar.
2. Pick a section from the list.
3. Make your change and click its save button. Most sections save card by card, not all at once.

passages.title: Settings
passages.heading: Who can change what
passages.text: Many settings are for admins only: inviting and removing people, Stripe, giving pages, custom fields, receipts, the audit log and the team two-factor rule. Staff can see most sections, but those controls are missing or greyed out for them. If your subscription has lapsed, saves are greyed out with "Reactivate your subscription to make changes."

passages.title: Settings
passages.heading: Where to go next
passages.text: See Connect Stripe, Connect your inbox and calendar, Run year-end receipts, Set up two-factor and Import donors for step-by-step help.

passages.title: The donor profile
passages.text: The profile is one person's whole story: every gift, every hour, every conversation, their next step and your tools.

passages.title: The donor profile
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
The header has their photo, name and stage, any flags such as Do not contact, and three buttons: "Log a call", "Plan a follow-up" and "More ▾". Below them sit their figures: Lifetime, This year, Last gift, Average gift, their first and largest gift, Last met and Last email. Click any of them to see the rows behind it.
The tabs are Overview, Gifts & pledges, Asks & pipeline, Conversations, Emails, Tasks, Notes, Funds, Related and Files. Overview has the timeline, giving by year, recent conversations and their household.
The rail on the right always shows their next step, contact details, relationship owner, journey and quick actions.

passages.title: The donor profile
passages.heading: Log a call
passages.text:
1. Click "Log a call".
2. Fill in what happened. Add a gift if one came with it.
3. Save it. It joins their timeline.

passages.title: The donor profile
passages.heading: Record a gift
passages.text:
1. Open "Gifts & pledges" and click "+ Add Gift".
2. Enter the amount, date, type and payment method. Pick a campaign or a pledge it fulfills if it has one.
3. Tick "Acknowledgement sent" if you have already thanked them.
4. Click "Save".
5. Click "Send receipt" on the row to email a tax receipt.

passages.title: The donor profile
passages.heading: Add a task
passages.text: 1. Click "More ▾", then "Add a task". Their open tasks are on the Tasks tab.

passages.title: The donor profile
passages.heading: More
passages.text: "More ▾" holds "Request a gift" (a link the donor can give through), drafting help such as "Draft an email" and "Brief me", "Record a video thank-you", "Add a task", "Impact summary", "Send their page link" and "Edit record". For admins it also holds "Export this person's data" and "Erase this person". See Export or erase a donor. A draft is only a draft: nothing reaches the donor until you send it.

passages.title: Organization and Team
passages.text: Organization holds your name, mission, staff and brand; Team holds who can sign in.

passages.title: Organization and Team
passages.heading: Organization
passages.text:
The first card shows your own name, email and role, and your organization's name and mission. "Staff and board" lists the people you have marked as staff or board. To add one, open their record and tap the Staff and board chip under their name.
Under "Brand Identity", drop in your logo, pick your color and click "Save branding". "Reset to Steward gold" undoes the color.

passages.title: Organization and Team
passages.heading: Invite someone
passages.text:
1. Open Team and click "+ Invite Staff". Only admins see this.
2. Type their email address.
3. Pick a role: Staff can view and edit data. Volunteer coordinator sees volunteers and hours only. Admin has full access, including settings.
4. Click "Generate invite link" and send the link to them yourself.

passages.title: Organization and Team
passages.heading: Remove someone
passages.text:
1. Find them in "Team Members" and click "Remove".
2. Read the confirm and agree. They can no longer sign in, records they wrote keep their name, and their donors become unassigned.

passages.title: Organization and Team
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: You cannot remove yourself. Every plan lets you add as many people as you need.

passages.title: Connections
passages.text: Connections is the one page for every outside service: setting it up, and checking it is still working.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
At the top, one line says how many services are connected and how many need attention. Click either number to see just those cards; click "Show every connection" to go back.
Then six sections, always in this order: Giving (Stripe, PayPal, Givebutter, Donorbox, Zeffy, Cash App, Venmo and statement imports), Email and calendar (Gmail and Outlook, and the BCC address), Email marketing (Mailchimp, Constant Contact), Books (QuickBooks, Xero and the bookkeeper file), Point of sale (Square, Toast) and Build your own (API keys, webhooks and Zapier).
Every card says the same things: what the service does, and its status. "Connected" shows when it last synced, "Not connected" means nothing comes through it, and "Needs attention" is in brass with the reason.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Connect, manage or fix
passages.text:
1. Find the service's card.
2. Click "Connect" to set it up. Some open the service's own sign-in page; others ask for a key, with "Test" to try it before you save.
3. Click "Manage" on a connected card to see what came through it, open its "History" (every check, newest first), or "Check now".
4. Click "Fix" on a card that needs attention. It opens the same detail with the reason at the top.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text:
Donorbox has no direct connection yet. Its card is in Giving, but it does not connect to Donorbox: its one button, "Import a file", brings in Donorbox's gift export as a statement. Nothing comes in from Donorbox on its own.
For a bookkeeping tool, "Manage" opens "Where the money posts", where "Save the mapping" says which account each fund goes to. For an email tool, "Preview" shows what the read would bring in, then "Save and read" (or "Save, read and add people").
Your donation form's QR code and embed code are not connections. They are in Fundraising, under Giving pages and forms. Settings used to have a separate Integrations section; it is part of this page now, and old links to it land here.

passages.title: Giving Pages
passages.text: Giving Pages is where you create the pages donors give through, and set your time zone and processing fees.

passages.title: Giving Pages
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
Three cards: "Time Zone", "Let Donors Cover Processing Costs" and "Giving Pages". Your pages are listed with "Edit" and "Archive". Archived pages can be restored with "Reactivate". Fundraising lists the same pages with links to open and copy.
You need Stripe connected for a page to take card gifts. See Connect Stripe.

passages.title: Giving Pages
passages.heading: Create a giving page
passages.text:
1. Click "+ New Giving Page". Only admins see it.
2. Fill in the page.
3. Click "Create giving page".
4. To change it later, click "Edit", then "Save changes", or "Edit in editor" to change the page's words and layout in the page editor, where nothing changes for donors until you publish.

passages.title: Giving Pages
passages.heading: Let donors cover the fees
passages.text:
1. Under "Let Donors Cover Processing Costs", click "Enable donor-covers-fees".
2. Donors then see an option to add the processing cost to their gift. Click "Disable donor-covers-fees" to turn it off.

passages.title: Giving Pages
passages.heading: Set your time zone
passages.text: 1. Under "Time Zone", pick your organization's zone. Only an admin can change it.

passages.title: Customization and Your words
passages.text: Customization adds your own fields and impact metrics; Your words sets what Steward calls things.

passages.title: Customization and Your words
passages.heading: Add a custom field
passages.text:
1. Open Customization. Under "Custom Fields", choose "Donor fields" or "Gift fields".
2. Click "+ Add Field". Only admins see it.
3. Name the field and pick its type. The type cannot change after you create it.
4. Save it. Use ↑ and ↓ to change the order.

passages.title: Customization and Your words
passages.heading: Retire a field
passages.text:
Click "Archive". Fields are never deleted, so the values already stored are kept. Open "Archived" and click "Restore" to bring one back.
If some stored values do not fit their field's type, a card lists them with a "Fix" button for each.

passages.title: Customization and Your words
passages.heading: Impact metrics
passages.text:
1. Under "Impact Metrics", click "+ Add Metric".
2. Name it, set the gift amount it starts at, and write the outcome sentence, for example what that gift pays for.
3. Save it. Use "Edit" or "Delete" later.

passages.title: Customization and Your words
passages.heading: Your words
passages.text: These are the questions you answered when you started: what you call your donors, your monthly givers and so on. Change an answer here and Steward uses your word across the app. Your words never change a receipt, a year-end statement or the donor portal.

passages.title: Tax Receipts
passages.text: Tax Receipts holds your legal details and turns receipts on, and is where you run year-end statements.

passages.title: Tax Receipts
passages.heading: Set up receipts
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Tax Receipts.
2. Fill in "Legal name", "EIN" and "Receipt address". These three are required.
3. If you want, add "Signature name (optional)", "Signature title (optional)" and "Custom message (optional)". Write {{donor_name}} in the message to use the donor's name.
4. Click "Save settings".
5. Click "Enable receipts". The badge changes to Enabled.
6. Click "Preview receipt" to see a sample receipt as a PDF.

passages.title: Tax Receipts
passages.heading: What happens next
passages.text:
Online gifts through your giving pages are receipted automatically. For a gift you record by hand, click "Send receipt" on the gift's row in the donor's Gifts & pledges tab.
The sample in "Preview receipt" is a single gift receipt for a made-up donor, not a year-end statement.

passages.title: Tax Receipts
passages.heading: Turn receipts off
passages.text: Click "Disable receipts". Receipts already sent are kept.

passages.title: Tax Receipts
passages.heading: Year-end statements
passages.text: The "Year-End Giving Statements" card is for admins and appears once receipts are enabled. It never runs on its own in January; you start it each year. See Run year-end receipts.

passages.title: Imports
passages.text: Imports is the record of every file you have brought in, with what each one added.

passages.title: Imports
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
A table of every import, newest first: its name, date, who ran it, rows in, gifts created and dollars in. Open a row to see the receipt it showed when it finished. If an import does not add up, the row says "Does not reconcile" so you can open it and see why.
This page is a record. It does not undo an import, and there is no import button here. To import, go to Donors and use "↑ Import & tools ▾". See Import donors.

passages.title: Imports
passages.heading: Add photos
passages.text:
1. Under "Add photos", click "Choose a folder".
2. Pick a folder of headshots. Steward matches each photo to a person by email, old-system ID or full name.

passages.title: Imports
passages.heading: Moving from another system
passages.text: If you are moving from another database, a card asks whether you have moved. Click "Yes, we've moved" once you have stopped using the old one, or "Not yet". You can change your answer later.

passages.title: Audit log
passages.text: The audit log is every change anyone made, who made it and when. Only admins can open it.

passages.title: Audit log
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text:
Each change in your organization is one row: who did it, what they did and when. That includes sign-ins, role changes and downloads of donor files, as well as edits to records. Rows cannot be changed or removed, by anyone.
Someone who is not an admin sees "The audit log is available to your organization's admins."

passages.title: Audit log
passages.heading: Find a change
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Audit log.
2. Use the filters at the top to narrow the list.
3. Click "What changed" on a row to see the before and after. Click "Hide what changed" to close it.
4. Click "Clear" to reset the filters.

passages.title: Audit log
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: Finance has its own audit log under Exports, with "Export CSV", for the money side. Changes the Agent made are listed in Agent, under Guardrails, where each can be undone for thirty days.

passages.title: Your Data and Account
passages.text: Your Data exports everything you hold; Account holds billing, notifications, your sending address and sign out.

passages.title: Your Data and Account
passages.heading: Export your data
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Your Data.
2. Click "Export all data (CSV)" (admins) or "Export as JSON".
3. When it says "Your export is ready.", the file downloads. "Download it again" fetches it a second time.

passages.title: Your Data and Account
passages.heading: Other things on Your Data
passages.text: "Reading and drafting" is the one switch for all of Steward's AI: check reading, drafts, briefs, scores, board summaries, Ask Steward and voice memos. Only admins can change it. When it is off, nothing is sent to Anthropic or OpenAI, and each of those features says "AI is turned off for your organization" and shows what it can without AI. "Demo Data" loads or clears sample donors so you can try things safely.

passages.title: Your Data and Account
passages.heading: Account
passages.text: Billing shows your plan and card, with "Manage billing →", "Choose a plan →" and "Cancel subscription". "Email notifications" lets you choose which emails you get: gifts to your donors, task assignments, the daily reminder, The Thread, and "Your meetings today", which is off unless you tick it and sends you, and only you, the same meeting briefs Home shows. "Show other income on the board dashboard" adds one figure you keep elsewhere, shown beside giving and never added to it. "Sign out" is at the bottom.

passages.title: Your Data and Account
passages.heading: Send from your own address
passages.text:
1. Under "Send from your own address", type the address you want mail to come from and click "Use this address". Admins only.
2. Add the records shown to your domain's DNS. "Copy" copies each value.
3. Click "Check". It can take a few minutes for the records to be seen.
4. "Use Steward's address instead" goes back to the default.

passages.title: Your Data and Account
passages.heading: Your voice
passages.text: Paste a few of your own thank-yous under "Your voice, for the thank-yous Steward drafts" and click "Save my voice".

passages.title: Security
passages.text: Security holds two-factor sign-in, the team rule, where you are signed in, and your password.

passages.title: Security
passages.heading: What you see
passages.text: "Two-factor sign-in" says whether it is on for you. Admins also see "Require two-factor for everyone on the team" and a "Your team" card with each person's two-factor state. "Where you're signed in" lists every browser used in the last week. "Change your password" is at the bottom.

passages.title: Security
passages.heading: Sign out a lost device
passages.text:
1. Under "Where you're signed in", find the browser you do not recognize.
2. Click "Sign out" on that row, or "Sign out everywhere else" to end every session but this one.

passages.title: Security
passages.heading: Change your password
passages.text:
1. Type your current password.
2. Type a new one of 8 or more characters.
3. Click "Change password". Every other session is signed out.

passages.title: Security
passages.heading: For admins
passages.text:
1. Turn on two-factor for yourself first. Steward will not let you require it otherwise.
2. Tick "Require two-factor for everyone on the team". People without it set it up the next time they sign in.
3. If someone loses their phone, click "Reset two-factor" beside them. This ends their sessions and emails them.
4. "Sign out everywhere" beside a person ends all of their sessions.

passages.title: Security
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: See Set up two-factor for the step-by-step. Security also has a "Download everything" card for admins, which downloads all your data as JSON.

passages.title: Import donors
passages.text: Your donors are the people who already believe in you, so this is where Steward starts: bring them, and their gift history if you have it, from a spreadsheet or another system.

passages.title: Import donors
passages.heading: Before you start
passages.text: Steward reads .csv, .tsv, .xlsx and .xls files. You can also paste CSV text and click "Parse →". Steward has a short how-to for exporting from your old donor system.

passages.title: Import donors
passages.heading: Import
passages.text:
1. Open Donors and click "↑ Import & tools ▾".
2. Choose "Import + History" (recommended) to bring gifts too, or "Import donors only".
3. Under "Where are your donors today?", pick your old system and read its short how-to, then click "Continue". Or click "Skip this, I already have my file ready".
4. Click "Choose your spreadsheet, or drag it here". If the workbook has a donors sheet and a gifts sheet, Steward offers to import both.
5. Check the mapping. Steward says what it detected. Click "✦ Auto-map" or set each column yourself.
6. For every column you have not mapped, choose "Store it" or "Discard". The import waits until each one is decided.
7. Click "Import" with the counts shown, for example "Import 412 donors + 1,906 gifts →".
8. Read the result. Duplicates are matched to existing people, and each merge has "Undo". Click "Done".

passages.title: Import donors
passages.heading: Afterwards
passages.text:
Every import is listed in Settings, under Imports, with what it added and whether it adds up. That page is a record and does not undo an import.
To add gifts for people already on file, use "Add giving history" from the same menu. "Merge duplicates" is there too.

passages.title: Connect Stripe
passages.text: Connect Stripe so your giving pages can take card gifts, paid straight to your organization's own Stripe account. Steward never holds the money.

passages.title: Connect Stripe
passages.heading: What it does
passages.text: Steward creates a Stripe Express account for your organization and Stripe pays you directly. Steward never touches your money. Only an admin can do this. Have your bank details to hand.

passages.title: Connect Stripe
passages.heading: Connect
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Connections.
2. On the Stripe card under Giving, click "Connect".
3. Stripe's own pages open. Fill in your organization's details and bank account and finish every step.
4. Stripe sends you back to Steward's Home screen.
5. Go back to Settings, Connections. Once Stripe says your account can take donations, the Stripe card says "Connected". Click "Manage" to see your account number and the date.

passages.title: Connect Stripe
passages.heading: If you stop part way
passages.text: Until Stripe has everything it needs, the Stripe card says "Needs attention" and "Stripe setup isn't finished". Click "Fix" to pick up where you left off on the same account.

passages.title: Connect Stripe
passages.heading: Check it is working
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Connections.
2. Find the Stripe card. Under "Take gifts on your giving pages" it should say it is on.
3. Make a small gift on your giving page and check it appears on the donor's record.

passages.title: Connect Stripe
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: Accounts are set up for the United States. "Read your Stripe history" on the Connections card is a separate, read-only connection.

passages.title: Connect your inbox and calendar
passages.text: Let your inbox and calendar keep the record, so every email and meeting with a donor lands on their timeline and nothing slips through the cracks.

passages.title: Connect your inbox and calendar
passages.heading: What Steward reads
passages.text:
Emails with people already in Steward, and meetings where one of them is invited: who, when, the subject and the body. It never reads mail with people who are not in Steward, does not open attachments (it only notes them), and never sends, deletes or moves an email. It adds to your calendar only when you book a visit from a donor's record.
Each person connects their own inbox.

passages.title: Connect your inbox and calendar
passages.heading: Connect
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Connections, and find the "Gmail and Outlook" card under "Email and calendar". Click "Connect".
2. Click "Connect Gmail and Google Calendar" or "Connect Outlook and Microsoft 365".
3. Sign in to Google or Microsoft and allow access.
4. Back in Steward, you see what was logged: emails from the last two years, meetings from a month back to two months ahead, and how many people now have a history.

passages.title: Connect your inbox and calendar
passages.heading: Keep some mail private
passages.text:
1. Under "Never log these", type an email address or a whole domain.
2. Click "Add". Click "Remove" to take one off.

passages.title: Connect your inbox and calendar
passages.heading: Pause or disconnect
passages.text: Each connected mailbox shows what was read and logged lately. If a read failed, "Check again" tries straight away and "Reconnect" signs in again. "Pause" stops reading until you click "Turn back on". "Disconnect" stops it and keeps what was logged. "Disconnect and remove" also deletes what it logged, and cannot be undone.

passages.title: Connect your inbox and calendar
passages.heading: Rather not connect
passages.text: Use your organization's BCC address instead: BCC it on any email to a donor and the email lands on their record. Find it under "Log an email by BCC", with a "Copy" button. A message that names nobody on file is held for you to place, or stored nowhere.

passages.title: Thank a gift
passages.text: Every gift deserves a thank-you from a person. Steward drafts it, and you send it from your own mail.

passages.title: Thank a gift
passages.heading: How it works
passages.text: When a gift is recorded, Steward drafts a thank-you and puts it on Home under "Thank-yous ready". Steward does not send it. It goes from your own mail. Donors marked deceased or do not contact are skipped.

passages.title: Thank a gift
passages.heading: Thank by email
passages.text:
1. On Home, find "Thank-yous ready".
2. Click "Read the draft".
3. Click "Copy" and paste it into a new email to the donor. Change any words you like there.
4. Send it from your own email.
5. Back in Steward, click "Mark sent". The gift is marked thanked and the thank-you is logged. Click "Skip" if you are thanking them another way.

passages.title: Thank a gift
passages.heading: Thank by letter
passages.text:
1. Open Fundraising, then Money in, then Acknowledgments. It lists gifts nobody has marked thanked.
2. Choose a template and tick the gifts. Gifts with a postal address are ticked for you.
3. Click "Preview", then "Print letters" and, if you want, "Mailing labels".
4. Sign and post the letters, then click "Mark as sent".

passages.title: Thank a gift
passages.heading: Already thanked them
passages.text: Tick "Acknowledgement sent" when you add the gift on the donor's Gifts & pledges tab, or tick Ack on the gift row later.

passages.title: Thank a gift
passages.heading: Make the drafts sound like you
passages.text: Click "Teach Steward your voice →", or open Settings, Account, paste a few of your own thank-yous and click "Save my voice".

passages.title: Thank a gift
passages.heading: Not the same as a receipt
passages.text: A tax receipt is separate: "Send receipt" on the gift row emails it directly.

passages.title: Send a video thank-you
passages.text: Record a short video for one donor on their record. Steward saves it and drafts the email with the link; you read the draft and send it.

passages.title: Send a video thank-you
passages.heading: How it works
passages.text:
A video thank-you is up to two minutes, recorded with your computer's or phone's camera. Saving it stores the video and puts one draft email to the donor, with the link in it, in Communications under "Drafts to review". Nothing is sent until you send it.
The donor opens the link to a small page in your organization's colors with the video on it. The link is the only way in, and nothing else about the donor is on the page.

passages.title: Send a video thank-you
passages.heading: Record one
passages.text:
1. Open the donor's record and click "More".
2. Click "Record a video thank-you". Your browser asks to use the camera and microphone the first time; allow it.
3. Click "Start recording". The time left shows while you record, and it stops by itself at two minutes. Click "Stop" when you are done.
4. Watch it back. Click "Record again" if you want another take.
5. Click "Save and draft the email". Click "Open the page the donor will see" to check it, then "Done".

passages.title: Send a video thank-you
passages.heading: Send it
passages.text:
1. Open Communications, then "Drafts to review".
2. Read the draft. Change any words you like.
3. Send it.

passages.title: Send a video thank-you
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text:
"Record a video thank-you" is greyed out when the donor has no email address, is marked deceased or do not contact, or when you have read-only access.
On a phone without in-browser recording, the button opens your phone's own camera instead. A video must be WebM or MP4 and two minutes or less.
Videos you recorded before are listed under "Recorded before" in the same window, each with "Watched" and the date once the donor has played it, or "Not watched yet". Playing the video is what counts as watched; a mail scanner opening the link does not.

passages.title: Run year-end receipts
passages.text: Send every donor one statement of what they gave last year, for their taxes, when you choose to.

passages.title: Run year-end receipts
passages.heading: Before you start
passages.text: Receipts must be set up and enabled in Settings, under Tax Receipts, with your legal name, EIN and receipt address. Only an admin can run statements. Steward never runs them on its own: you start the run each year.

passages.title: Run year-end receipts
passages.heading: Run the statements
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Tax Receipts, and scroll to "Year-End Giving Statements".
2. Check "Tax year". It starts on last year.
3. Click "Dry run". Steward shows how many donors and gifts it found, and how many donors have no email address. Nothing is sent.
4. Fix any missing emails you can on those donors' records, and run the dry run again.
5. Click "Generate & send" and confirm. This sends real emails.
6. Read the result: how many statements were made, emailed and skipped.

passages.title: Run year-end receipts
passages.heading: Donors with no email
passages.text: Their statement is still made, just not emailed, so plan to reach them another way.

passages.title: Run year-end receipts
passages.heading: One donor at a time
passages.text:
1. Open the donor and go to "Gifts & pledges".
2. Click "Year-end statement", choose the "Tax year", and click "Generate & email".
3. It replaces any earlier statement for that year.

passages.title: Run year-end receipts
passages.heading: Good to know
passages.text: There is no preview of a real statement before the bulk send, so try one donor first if you want to see it. Finance has a Year-end statements card that brings you back here.

passages.title: Set up two-factor
passages.text: Two-factor asks for a six-digit code as well as your password, so a stolen password is not enough.

passages.title: Set up two-factor
passages.heading: Turn it on
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Security, and find "Two-factor sign-in".
2. Click "Use an authenticator app" or "Use a code by email".
3. For an app, scan the QR code with your authenticator, or type the key shown. For email, open the code Steward sent you. It lasts 10 minutes.
4. Type the six-digit code and click "Turn it on".
5. Save your ten recovery codes with "Copy" or "Download". They are shown once only.

passages.title: Set up two-factor
passages.heading: Signing in
passages.text:
1. Enter your email and password and click "Sign In →".
2. Type the six-digit code from your app or your email.
3. Tick "Trust this browser for 30 days" on a computer only you use.

passages.title: Set up two-factor
passages.heading: Lost your phone
passages.text:
Type one of your recovery codes instead of the six-digit code. Each works once, and Steward emails you when one is used. If you have none left, ask an admin to click "Reset two-factor" beside your name.
Five wrong codes in a row pause code entry for 15 minutes, and Steward emails you.

passages.title: Set up two-factor
passages.heading: Manage it later
passages.text: In Security, type a current code to use "Make new recovery codes" (the old set stops working) or "Turn two-factor off". If your organization requires two-factor, it stays on.

passages.title: Set up two-factor
passages.heading: Require it for the team
passages.text: Admins: turn it on for yourself, then tick "Require two-factor for everyone on the team". Anyone without it sets it up at their next sign-in.

passages.title: Export or erase a donor
passages.text: Give a person a copy of what you hold about them, or remove them for good while your books still add up.

passages.title: Export or erase a donor
passages.heading: Export one person's data
passages.text:
1. Open the person's record. You need to be an admin.
2. Click "More ▾", then "Export this person's data".
3. A JSON file named after them downloads at once.

passages.title: Export or erase a donor
passages.heading: What the export holds
passages.text: Their profile, gifts, pledges, receipts, logged notes, emails and meetings, calendar meetings, event attendance, volunteer hours, custom fields, relationships, and their email preferences. It does not include tasks or thank-you drafts. The download is recorded in the audit log.

passages.title: Export or erase a donor
passages.heading: Erase a person
passages.text:
1. Open the person's record. You need to be an admin.
2. Click "More ▾", then "Erase this person".
3. Read what will happen.
4. Type ERASE in capitals in the box.
5. Click "Erase for good", or "Cancel".

passages.title: Export or erase a donor
passages.heading: What erase removes and keeps
passages.text:
Removed for good: their name, contact details, notes, tags, photo, custom fields, and every logged email, meeting and conversation, along with their tasks, drafts and journey steps. Their name is scrubbed from gift notes and from receipts already made.
Kept: their gifts, as anonymous gifts, so your books, issued receipts and every total still match to the cent. The record stays as "Erased person". If they asked not to be emailed, their address stays on your do-not-email list so they are never mailed again. The audit log notes that an erasure happened, not what was erased.
This cannot be undone. Export first if the person asked for a copy.

passages.title: Auctions
passages.text: Auctions runs an online auction with its own public page: donated items, bidding that opens and closes on time, and winners who pay through your own Stripe account.

passages.title: Auctions
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: Auctions sits under Fundraising, in Campaigns & pages, and has its own entry in the sidebar under Raise. An auction can belong to an event or stand on its own. Each auction has a public page where people register to bid with their name, email and phone. Steward keeps the items, who is winning, who won, whether they have paid and who registered, and it prepares the notes you send. Nothing here sends by itself and nothing here moves money.

passages.title: Auctions
passages.heading: Start an auction
passages.text:
1. Click "New auction".
2. Give it a "Title", and choose "Part of an event (optional)" or leave it "On its own".
3. Set "Bidding opens" and "Bidding closes", and add "What it is for".
4. Click "Create auction". The auction opens, with its public page link at the top.

passages.title: Auctions
passages.heading: Add an item
passages.text:
1. Inside the auction, click "Add an item".
2. Fill in the "Title", "Category", "Donated by" (a name already on file), "Fair market value", "Starting bid" and "Bid increment". "Buy now (optional)" is there if you want it.
3. Add a "Description" and up to five photos. The first photo is the main one.
4. Click "Save item". Once an item has a donor and a fair market value, "Record as in-kind gift" records the donation on that person's record.

passages.title: Auctions
passages.heading: Close out the winners
passages.text:
1. When bidding closes, each item's winner appears under "Winners": the highest bid, and between equal bids, the earliest.
2. If someone won in the room, click "Record the winner" on the item, pick "Who won it" and the "Winning bid", then "Save the winner".
3. Under "Notes to bidders", click "Prepare the winners' emails". Steward writes a draft for each winner with their pay link. Read each one and press "Send", or "Send all" when there are several. "Preview the winner email" shows what the winner sees.
4. "Copy pay link" gives you a winner's link to share another way.

passages.title: Auctions
passages.heading: Remind bidders before it closes
passages.text:
1. While the auction is open, click "Prepare "bidding closes soon"" under "Notes to bidders".
2. Read the drafts and press "Send" on each, or "Send all".

passages.title: Auctions
passages.heading: What the numbers mean
passages.text:
Raised: every payment a winner has made for an item in this auction, at the amount charged: the gift their payment recorded.
Won, paid or not: the winning bid on every item whose bidding has closed, whether the winner has paid yet or not.
Items sold: every item whose bidding has closed with a winning bid, with that bid.
Items unsold: every item whose bidding has closed with no bid at all. An item still open is neither sold nor unsold.
Bidders: every registered bidder who placed at least one bid, largest total of winning bids first.
Click any of these numbers to see the items or people behind it.

passages.title: Auctions
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward never charges a winner and never sends a note on its own: winners pay on your own Stripe account, and every note waits for your Send. Without Stripe connected, winners cannot pay online, so take their payment as you would any gift. Steward does not issue refunds. If a payment needs refunding, the screen lists it under "Payments to refund"; refund it in Stripe, then click "I refunded this in Stripe". "Archive" takes the public page down and keeps every bid and winner.

passages.title: Brand kit
passages.text: The brand kit holds the colors, signature, address and tax language that every template, printed letter and receipt uses.

passages.title: Brand kit
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: The brand kit lives in Settings. Set it once and every template, printed letter and receipt reads it: two colors from a safe palette, the signature block, your organization's address and the tax language. Your logo is the logo you already uploaded.

passages.title: Brand kit
passages.heading: Choose your colors
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Brand kit.
2. Pick a "Main color" and a "Second color". Only colors that stay readable on paper and on screen are offered.
3. Click "Save brand kit".

passages.title: Brand kit
passages.heading: Set the signature and address
passages.text:
1. Under "Signature block", fill in the "Signer name" and "Signer title". "Another signature line" adds a second signer.
2. Add one more line if you want, such as a phone number or a P.S.
3. Check the "Organization address".
4. Click "Save brand kit". From then on, every template, printed letter and receipt uses it.

passages.title: Brand kit
passages.heading: Set your tax language
passages.text:
1. Under "Tax language", write the sentence printed at the foot of every receipt and statement. Your EIN follows it.
2. Left empty, Steward uses the sentence shown in grey.

passages.title: Brand kit
passages.heading: Preview a letter with a real person
passages.text:
1. Under "Preview with a real person", find a person to preview with.
2. Look at the letter with their details filled in.
3. "Print for this person" downloads it, ready to print. "Make a draft for this person" puts it in your drafts to review; nothing is sent.

passages.title: Brand kit
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward does not let you pick a color that would be hard to read, and it never sends a letter from here. Changes are not used until you save them; the screen says "Changed, not saved" until you do.

passages.title: Data health
passages.text: Data health finds the tidying your records need, such as duplicates, messy addresses, people who moved and emails that bounce, and lets you fix each with one approval.

passages.title: Data health
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: Data health is a view of Donors, beside Directory, Re-engage and Map. It shows one line for each kind of mess: a count that opens its rows, a sentence that says what the count is, and the one action that fixes it. Steward suggests, and a person approves. Nothing changes until you press the button, and a merge can be undone for 30 days.

passages.title: Data health
passages.heading: Merge duplicates
passages.text:
1. On "Possible duplicates", click "Review pairs". Each pair carries a High, Medium or Low confidence.
2. Click "Compare" to see the two records side by side, then "Compare and merge" to choose which record to keep. "Keep the other record instead" swaps them.
3. If they are not the same person, click "Not a duplicate".
4. "Merge all high-confidence pairs" merges every high-confidence pair at once. Pairs from two different households are left for you to merge one at a time.
5. Under "Recent merges", "Undo" brings back both records and every gift, note and row that moved, for 30 days.

passages.title: Data health
passages.heading: Tidy addresses
passages.text:
1. On "Addresses to tidy", click "Review changes".
2. Each address is shown the standard US way: street words shortened the postal way, units on their own line, two-letter states, ZIP+4 written with a dash, capitals fixed. This is worked out on Steward's own server; no address is sent anywhere.
3. Approve the ones that look right, or skip them. Addresses Steward cannot read are flagged rather than guessed at; open the person to fix those by hand.

passages.title: Data health
passages.heading: Update people who moved
passages.text:
1. On "People who moved", click "Prepare or bring in a file".
2. Prepare an address update file and send it to a change-of-address provider you choose.
3. When the provider sends results back, bring them in here and click "Review moves" to approve each new address.

passages.title: Data health
passages.heading: Fix emails
passages.text:
1. On "Emails to look at", click "Review emails". These bounce, are not valid, look like a typo, or are a shared office address on a person.
2. A suggested fix is filled in where one is obvious. Nothing changes until you save it.
3. A bounce mark stays until you confirm the new address is right with "Yes, clear the bounce mark".

passages.title: Data health
passages.heading: What the numbers mean
passages.text:
Possible duplicates: pairs that may be the same person, counted by high, medium and low confidence.
Addresses to tidy: addresses that can be written the standard US way, plus any that cannot be read and are listed for you to fix by hand.
People who moved: changes of address from the provider's file waiting for you.
Emails to look at: emails that bounce, are not valid, look like a typo, or are a shared office address on a person.
No way to reach: people with no email, no phone and no mailable address. Open a person to add one.

passages.title: Data health
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward does not merge, change an address or clear a bounce on its own. It does not run a change-of-address check for you: you send the prepared file to a provider of your choice and bring their results back.

passages.title: Memberships
passages.text: Memberships holds your membership levels, everyone who holds one, and who is coming up for renewal or has lapsed.

passages.title: Memberships
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: Memberships sits under Fundraising, in Campaigns & pages, and has its own entry in the sidebar under Raise. It shows your levels with their counts and every membership, sorted by when it expires. A membership payment is a gift, so it lands on the person's record with their other giving, and their receipt states the deductible part. Each person's own record also shows the membership they hold or held.

passages.title: Memberships
passages.heading: Add a level
passages.text:
1. Click "Add a level". Setting a level's price, the value of its benefits and its term is for an admin.
2. Give it a name, a price and a term: "12 months", "Calendar year", "Monthly" or "Lifetime", and whether it is "Individual" or "Household".
3. Enter the value of the benefits members receive. This is your number: Steward never estimates it, and at $0 receipts call the whole payment deductible.
4. Add a sentence or two for the card on your membership page, then click "Save level".

passages.title: Memberships
passages.heading: Put someone on a level
passages.text:
1. Open the person's record and find "Membership". If they are "Not a member yet.", click "Add a membership".
2. Choose the level and answer "How was it paid?".
3. Click "Record membership". To renew someone, click "Renew", then "Record renewal".
4. "Member card (PDF)" makes a printable card for them.

passages.title: Memberships
passages.heading: Share your membership page
passages.text:
1. Click "Copy page link" or "Open page". Your membership page lists every level that is for sale and not hidden, in the order shown here.
2. "Copy join link" gives you the link to send someone who wants to join.

passages.title: Memberships
passages.heading: Follow up on renewals and lapsed members
passages.text:
1. A renewal thread opens a set number of days before a membership expires, and an expired one stays in grace for a set number of days, then lapses. You choose both numbers on this screen.
2. Steward drafts the renewal note; nothing is sent until a person sends it.
3. Filter by "Lapsed" to see people whose most recent membership has lapsed and who hold none now.

passages.title: Memberships
passages.heading: What the numbers mean
passages.text:
Active, Grace and Lapsed members: each person counts once per membership. Active and in-grace members hold a current membership; lapsed ones have passed their grace period. Click a count to see the people.
Years as a member: the membership terms they held.
Still gives: a gift that was not a membership payment, so someone can be a lapsed member and a current donor at once.
Their page: whether the member has opened their own page, which holds their card, their renewal and their receipts.
"Directory CSV" downloads the member list for a spreadsheet.

passages.title: Memberships
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward does not send renewal reminders on its own: it drafts them, and your team sends. Cancelling a membership stops it; it does not refund the payment, which is its own step on the gift.

passages.title: Peer-to-peer
passages.text: Peer-to-peer is where you run a walk, a ride or any campaign where supporters raise money on their own pages, alone or in teams.

passages.title: Peer-to-peer
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: Peer-to-peer sits under Fundraising, in Campaigns & pages, and has its own entry in the sidebar under Raise. A peer-to-peer campaign is a giving page with peer-to-peer turned on. Supporters sign up from the public page, make their own fundraiser page, and can start or join a team. This screen shows one campaign at a time: what it has raised, every team and fundraiser against their goal, and who has not raised anything yet, so someone can pick up the phone.

passages.title: Peer-to-peer
passages.heading: Start a campaign
passages.text:
1. Click "New peer-to-peer campaign".
2. Fill in the "Name", and if you want, a "Goal ($)" and "Ends on" date.
3. Check the "Public page address". It comes from the name, and if it is taken, Steward adds a number.
4. Tick "New fundraiser pages need approval before they go public" if you want to see each page first.
5. Click "Make the campaign". An existing giving page that is "Not peer-to-peer yet" can be switched on with "Turn it on".

passages.title: Peer-to-peer
passages.heading: Add a team or a fundraiser yourself
passages.text:
1. Under Teams, click "Add a team", give it a name and a goal, and save.
2. Under Fundraisers, click "Add a fundraiser", type "Their name", "Their email", a goal and a team if there is one, then click "Add".
3. Steward finds the person by email, or adds them as a new person. Nobody is emailed. Use "Copy their manage link" to pass the link on yourself.
