passages.title: Peer-to-peer
passages.heading: Encourage the people who have not started
passages.text:
1. Look at the card that says how many fundraisers have not raised anything yet. It lists them by name.
2. Open a fundraiser's options to see a suggested note, and click "Open in my mail" to write it from your own email.
3. If you need approval on, new pages wait for you: click "Approve" on each. "Take it down" hides a page and "Put it back" restores it.

passages.title: Peer-to-peer
passages.heading: What the numbers mean
passages.text:
Raised: everything given through this campaign's page, added up from the gift rows themselves.
Through people: what came in through fundraisers' own pages.
Given directly: what was given to the campaign page without a fundraiser.
Click "Raised" to see what it is made of: through teams, through fundraisers with no team, and given to the page directly. These three always add up to the total.
A fundraiser's Raised: every gift given through that fundraiser's own page, added up to the cent.
"Fundraisers CSV" downloads the list of fundraisers for a spreadsheet.

passages.title: Peer-to-peer
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward does not email your fundraisers for you. Notes open in your own mail, and adding a fundraiser sends nothing. A fundraiser is matched to a person in your records by exact email only; one shown as "no record matched" has no soft credit recorded until their email matches someone on file.

passages.title: Privacy
passages.text: Privacy lets an organization that serves clients keep their details out of Steward, and holds back health details found in anyone's email.

passages.title: Privacy
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: Some organizations serve people whose families are also donors, such as a therapy riding program. Privacy is for them. With the setting "We serve clients whose details are private" on, Steward will never bring in email, documents or notes about people you mark as clients, and it holds back health details it finds in anyone's email until you choose to keep them. With the setting off, nothing here runs.

passages.title: Privacy
passages.heading: Turn privacy mode on
passages.text:
1. Open Settings, then Privacy. Only an admin can change this.
2. Tick "We serve clients whose details are private".
3. A line on the Connections card then says privacy mode is on, how many people are marked as clients and how many health details were held back this month.

passages.title: Privacy
passages.heading: Mark people as clients
passages.text:
1. Click "Mark people as clients".
2. Type names or emails, or pick a group and click "Check this group".
3. Confirm the list. People already marked say so. "Undo" puts it back.
4. You can also tick "Client (never capture)" on one person's record.

passages.title: Privacy
passages.heading: See what was held back
passages.text:
1. Click the number of health details held back this month. Each one shows who and when, never what.
2. A held sentence is replaced on the stored email with the line "Mentioned a health matter. Open it in your mailbox."

passages.title: Privacy
passages.heading: What the numbers mean
passages.text:
People marked as clients: people who are never brought in from Gmail or Outlook, never logged from the BCC address, never a capture card and never a memo.
Health details held back this month: sentences about a person's health that Steward replaced with one neutral line before storing the email.

passages.title: Privacy
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward is not HIPAA compliant and has no business associate agreements, so do not rely on it for that. When your organization has Steward's AI turned off, it cannot check email for health details, so new email keeps only its date, who it was between and its subject.

passages.title: Recurring gifts
passages.text: Recurring is where every monthly and yearly gift lives: who gives, how much, what it supports, and which cards need rescue.

passages.title: Recurring gifts
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: Recurring sits under Fundraising, in Campaigns & pages. When a donor starts a recurring gift, or you propose one and they accept, it lands here. The cards that need you come first: past due, about to lapse and cards that just failed. Below them is every sustainer, with their amount, frequency, fund and next charge.

passages.title: Recurring gifts
passages.heading: Propose a recurring gift
passages.text:
1. Click "Propose a recurring gift".
2. Search for the donor by name or email.
3. Choose the amount and the frequency, "Monthly" or "Yearly", and a fund if you want one.
4. Click "Send to donor". The proposal shows as pending until the donor completes it. Nothing is charged until they accept.

passages.title: Recurring gifts
passages.heading: Help a donor whose card failed
passages.text:
1. Find them under "Needs recovery" or filter the roster by "Past due".
2. Click "Propose card update…" and then "Send card-update link". The donor updates their own card.
3. If the email did not go, Steward says so; resend it from the roster or tell them yourself.

passages.title: Recurring gifts
passages.heading: Pause, change or cancel a gift
passages.text:
1. Open the row for the gift.
2. Click "Pause" and, if you want, set an "Auto-resume date (optional)". A paused gift shows "Resume".
3. "Change fund designation…" changes what it supports, straight away.
4. To change the amount or frequency, click "Propose a change…". The donor confirms it themselves.
5. "Cancel subscription" stops it. A donor asking to stop is always honored, even if your subscription has lapsed.

passages.title: Recurring gifts
passages.heading: What the numbers mean
passages.text:
Monthly giving: every monthly gift charging successfully today, at what it brings in each month. A yearly gift counts as a twelfth of its amount.
Change in monthly giving: monthly gifts started since the date shown, at what each adds a month, less those that ended in the same time.
Cards updated automatically: monthly gifts still giving whose card the bank updated by itself since the date shown.
Months on file: every monthly gift charging successfully today, with how many months it has been giving.
Sustainer retention, 12 months: of the sustainers who started at least a year ago, how many are still giving a year in. It shows "Not set" until a subscription is a year old.

passages.title: Recurring gifts
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward never changes an amount, a frequency or a card itself: anything that moves money is an invitation the donor completes. Whether a card is updated automatically depends on the card network and on your own Stripe account; a card that is not updated still goes to failed-card recovery. Recurring gifts here are the ones running through your Stripe account; sustainers from an imported file are shown separately as "Sustainers from your file".

passages.title: Search
passages.text: The search box at the top of every screen finds any record in your organization: people, gifts, notes, meetings, campaigns, events, grants and more.

passages.title: Search
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: The search box sits in the top bar of every screen. Press ⌘K on a Mac, iPhone or iPad, or Ctrl K everywhere else, to jump to it from anywhere. On a phone, tap the magnifying glass at the top. It looks across everything your organization keeps: people (by name, email, phone or an organization's contact person), households, campaigns and appeals, events, giving pages, peer-to-peer pages, grants, auctions, membership levels, open tasks, saved reports and dashboards, past board reports, documents by file name, gifts, monthly plans, pledges, journeys, meetings, emails, notes and imports.

passages.title: Search
passages.heading: Find a person
passages.text:
1. Press ⌘K or Ctrl K, or click the search box.
2. Type part of a name, an email or a phone number. Two characters are enough to start.
3. Pick the person from the list to open their record.

passages.title: Search
passages.heading: Find a gift by amount or date
passages.text:
1. Type an amount, such as "$500", to see gifts, pledges and monthly plans of that amount.
2. Type a day, such as "Oct 3", to see that day's gifts and meetings.
3. Type a name and the word "gift", such as "Rafael gift", to see that person's gifts.

passages.title: Search
passages.heading: See everything of one kind
passages.text:
1. Each group shows its first few results.
2. Click "See all" on a group to see up to fifty of that kind.

passages.title: Search
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Search only ever looks in your own organization. Deleted records do not show: a person who was deleted takes their gifts, plans, pledges, meetings, emails and notes out of search with them, and an archived journey is left out. A volunteer coordinator does not have search, because almost everything it finds carries giving. Searching never changes anything.

passages.title: Set up Steward for me
passages.text: Set up Steward for me takes your donor files, your website and the tools you take gifts with, shows you a plan in plain sentences, and does the setup once you press Start.

passages.title: Set up Steward for me
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: This is the quickest way to get going. You give Steward three things: your donor files, your website, and how you take gifts. Steward shows you a plan before anything happens. When you press Start, it imports and checks your files to the cent, fills in your profile and branding, sets up your funds, starter groups, thank-you drafts in your words and journeys (paused), and prepares invitations for your team. At the end it tells you who to call tomorrow. You can also choose "Set it up yourself" and do each step by hand.

passages.title: Set up Steward for me
passages.heading: Start setup
passages.text:
1. Under "Your donor files", add your files. Any number, in any format the import reads: CSV or Excel, a Salesforce Contacts and Donations pair, DonorPerfect, Bloomerang, Neon, or a spreadsheet you kept.
2. Under "Your website", give your address. Steward reads a few public pages for your mission, logo, colors, address, EIN and team. Anything it is not sure of becomes a question.
3. Under "How you take gifts", tick the tools you use, such as Stripe, PayPal, Zeffy, Givebutter, Square or checks.
4. Click "Read my files and show me the plan".

passages.title: Set up Steward for me
passages.heading: Read the plan and press Start
passages.text:
1. Under "Here is the plan", read what Steward will do. Nothing has happened yet.
2. Answer any questions it asks. "Change what I gave" takes you back to the files.
3. Click "Start".
4. You can close the tab. Setup keeps going, and the page picks up where it is when you come back. If it stops, click "Carry on from where it stopped".

passages.title: Set up Steward for me
passages.heading: When Steward is ready
passages.text:
1. Read "What Steward did" and "Waiting on you".
2. Invitations for your team are "Prepared for your click": each one waits until you press "Send". Connections wait for you to press "Connect".
3. Click "Go to my home screen".

passages.title: Set up Steward for me
passages.heading: Undo everything
passages.text:
1. On the finished page, click "Undo all of setup".
2. This removes every person, gift, fund, template and journey setup made. Click "Yes, undo all of it" to confirm.

passages.title: Set up Steward for me
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Setup never emails anyone: team invitations wait for you to send them, and journeys are set up paused, so nothing reaches a donor until you turn it on. It does not connect your payment tools for you; signing in to each one is yours to do from Connections. Possible duplicates found on the way are left for you to review, now or later, from Data health.

passages.title: Tell Steward
passages.text: Tell Steward turns a few spoken or typed sentences about a meeting or a call into the paperwork: the conversation logged, the follow-up on your list, and anything sensitive held for your yes.

passages.title: Tell Steward
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: After lunch with a donor or a phone call, you can tell Steward what happened instead of filling in forms. Open it with the "Tell Steward" button on Home, "Tell Steward about" a person on their record, from the sidebar, or from More on a phone. Steward logs the conversation on each person it names, puts the follow-up on your list with its date and notes their interests. Those are listed under "Done for you", with one Undo. Anything that matters more waits under "Waiting for your yes": a drafted email, every amount, a contact change and any personal detail.

passages.title: Tell Steward
passages.heading: Tell Steward what happened
passages.text:
1. Click "Tell Steward".
2. On a phone, hold to talk, or tap and talk; release, or tap "Stop", when you are done. On a laptop, type what happened, or use your keyboard's microphone.
3. Read "What Steward heard" and change anything before you send.
4. Click "Send to Steward".

passages.title: Tell Steward
passages.heading: Check what Steward did
passages.text:
1. Under "Done for you", read each line. "Undo this memo" takes all of it back.
2. If Steward heard a name it could not place, "Find the person" or "Pick the person" lets you choose who it was, or add them as someone new.
3. Under "Waiting for your yes", look at each card. A drafted email opens with "Open the draft"; it is never sent from here. An amount, a contact change or a personal detail is only saved when you say yes.

passages.title: Tell Steward
passages.heading: When Steward could not file it
passages.text:
1. If Steward did not understand the memo, it says so and files nothing.
2. Click "Save as a note" and only the words you sent go on the person's record, as a note.

passages.title: Tell Steward
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward never keeps a recording, only the words you send. Nothing is sent to anyone: a drafted email waits in your drafts for you to read and send. Amounts are never recorded until you confirm them. When your organization has Steward's AI turned off, the memo is saved as a note on the person you pick, and nothing else is read from it.

passages.title: To confirm
passages.text: To confirm is one place for every gift that arrived on paper or as a document, waiting as a card until a person confirms it.

passages.title: To confirm
passages.heading: What this screen is for
passages.text: To confirm sits under Fundraising, in Money in. A photographed check, a scanned batch, a pledge form or a fund's grant letter each becomes a card here. Steward reads the image and fills in what it can: who it is from, the amount, the date and the fund. Money never lands on its own; it waits for you to check the card and confirm it. Small changes, like an updated address or a document filed on a profile, are done right away and listed under "Done for you", each with Undo for 30 days. The Fundraising entry in the sidebar shows how many cards are waiting.

passages.title: To confirm
passages.heading: Snap or drop in checks
passages.text:
1. On a phone, tap "Snap a check" and take the photo. Tap "Snap another check" for the next one.
2. On a laptop, drag check images or a scanned PDF onto the drop area, or browse for the files.
3. Each check becomes a card in "Waiting".

passages.title: To confirm
passages.heading: Confirm a card
passages.text:
1. Look at the image beside the form. "Open the full image" shows it larger.
2. Check who it is from. If more than one person in Steward could be this, pick one. If nobody matches, "It's someone new" adds them when you confirm.
3. Check the amount, the date and the fund. If the amount is blank, fill it in from the image.
4. Click the button, which names what you are logging, for example "Log $250 check". The gift is recorded and a thank-you draft is prepared for you to read and send from your thank-you list. Nothing is sent.

passages.title: To confirm
passages.heading: Skip a card, or bring one back
passages.text:
1. If a card is not a gift, click "Skip it" and choose a reason: "It isn't a gift", "It's a duplicate", "Already entered by hand" or "Something else".
2. Skipped cards stay under "Skipped" for 30 days. Open "Skipped" to bring one back.

passages.title: To confirm
passages.heading: What the numbers mean
passages.text:
Waiting: cards that have not been confirmed or skipped yet.
Skipped: cards a person skipped in the last 30 days.

passages.title: To confirm
passages.heading: What Steward doesn't do here
passages.text: Steward never logs money from a card by itself, and never sends a thank-you from here: the draft waits on your thank-you list. If a card is an employer's matching gift and Steward cannot find the original gift it matches, it cannot be logged yet; log the original gift first, or skip it. When a donor-advised fund's letter names an advisor who is not in Steward yet, no soft credit is added until you add them.

passages.title: Why Steward
passages.heading: The vision
passages.text: Small nonprofits run on relationships and lose them to turnover, spreadsheets and sheer overload. Someone gives from the heart, and a year later nobody remembers to call. Steward is the institutional memory of generosity: every donor, every conversation, every promise, held gently, so that no one who ever believed in the cause is forgotten by it.

passages.title: Why Steward
passages.heading: The six pillars
passages.text:
1. Never lose a single believer.
Every donor is someone who raised their hand for your mission. Steward notices who has gone quiet, not as a report you have to pull but as a tap on the shoulder. When you ask why, it shows the reasons in dollars, and every number opens the gifts and conversations behind it. Then it tells you who to call tomorrow morning and puts each step on your list for the day it's due. No one who ever believed in the cause is forgotten by it.

2. Technology that knows its place.
Every nonprofit leader has the same nightmare: software that says the wrong thing to the right donor. So we built the opposite. Steward remembers everything and assumes nothing. It drafts the note, suggests the call and prepares the brief, and it never sends, publishes or acts without your yes. It's the staff member who does all the homework and none of the talking out of turn. The relationship stays yours. It just never has to rely on your memory alone.

3. One home for everyone who believes.
Right now your people are scattered: donors in a spreadsheet, volunteers in another app, gala guests on a clipboard. But they're not separate people. The woman who gave $500 also worked Saturdays and brought two friends to the gala. Steward keeps one story per person, every gift, every hour, every conversation, so when you reach out you know the whole relationship, not just the last transaction. Your community isn't donors plus volunteers. It's people, whole people, with whole histories.

4. Numbers you can stand behind. 
When the board asks how the year went, you should be able to answer without a weekend in spreadsheets. Every figure in Steward opens the gifts behind it and adds up to the cent, so you can say it out loud and know it's true. Your story, told in numbers you trust.

5. You don't have to tear anything down.
The last thing an overstretched team needs is a migration project. So Steward doesn't ask for one. It connects to the tools you already use, your payments, your books, your email, and quietly watches them, so nothing slips through the cracks between systems. You keep your world. We just make sure nothing in it gets lost.

6. A partner, not a vendor. 
You'll talk to the person who built it. Month to month, no platform fee on your gifts, and Steward never holds or moves your money. If something isn't right, it gets fixed in days, not quarters. We'd rather earn your trust every month than lock it in for a year.

passages.title: Why Steward
passages.heading: The opening gift
passages.text: The free audit (Lost & Found) is a gift, not a hook: ten minutes, no pitch, their own file. Not "you're losing $47,000." Instead: "Here are the people who stood with you last year. Let's make sure none of them slip away unnoticed."

passages.title: Why Steward
passages.heading: Keep it true
passages.text: Every claim must be true on prod the day it ships. "Never sends without your yes" means the Agent and drafts; receipts and sequences an org has turned on are the org's own yes, so say "Steward never sends anything you haven't approved." "Connects to your books" only once QuickBooks is approved by Intuit and live for customers; until then say "payments and email". Prices stay off this copy until pricing is decided.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Stripe
passages.text: Stripe works today. Gifts and payouts flow in; every payout matched to its gifts. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Spreadsheets and CSV
passages.text: Spreadsheets and CSV works today. Any export, mapped once and remembered. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Bookkeeper file
passages.text: Bookkeeper file works today. A monthly gift file that foots to the cent. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Open API
passages.text: Open API works today. Scoped keys and webhooks for your own tools. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Mailchimp
passages.text: Mailchimp works today. Audiences and tags kept in step with Steward. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Gmail and Outlook
passages.text: Gmail and Outlook works today. Emails with donors land on their profile. Google shows a one-time unverified-app screen until our verification is finished. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: PayPal
passages.text: PayPal works today. Gifts come in and are watched for gaps. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Givebutter
passages.text: Givebutter works today. Campaign gifts pulled in. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Square
passages.text: Square works today. Sales and donations read in. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Xero
passages.text: Xero is not available yet. Each gift sent to your books as one bank transaction when you press Sync. Being verified with a first organization. It is built and being checked with a first organization before it is offered to everyone.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Donorbox
passages.text: Donorbox is not built. Once built: gifts and recurring plans pulled in. Settings, Connections has a Donorbox card in the Giving section, but it does not connect to Donorbox: its only button is "Import a file", for Donorbox's gift export as a statement file. Nothing comes in from Donorbox on its own.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: QuickBooks Online
passages.text: QuickBooks Online is not available yet. Direct connection. It is built and waiting on Intuit's approval before customers can connect it.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Zapier
passages.text: Zapier is not available yet. Connect hundreds of other tools. The Zapier app is built and waiting on Zapier's review before it is listed.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Constant Contact
passages.text: Constant Contact is not available yet. List sync. The sign-in is built, and it is waiting on Constant Contact's keys.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Forward-to-log email
passages.text: Forward-to-log email is not available yet. Copy a Steward address on any email to log it. It is built and waiting on a final check that a forwarded email lands on the right person.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Zeffy
passages.text: Zeffy works today. In Zeffy, an admin opens Settings, then Integrations, chooses API, and copies the key. Connect it in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Cash App
passages.text: Cash App works today. Cash App has no API that reads an account. Once a month you drop the statement in and Steward reads it. There is no live connection to read: you drop in its export or statement in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Venmo
passages.text: Venmo works today. Venmo has no API that reads an account. Once a month you drop the statement in and Steward reads it. There is no live connection to read: you drop in its export or statement in Settings, Connections.

passages.title: Connections
passages.heading: Toast
passages.text: Toast works today. Toast's API is behind their partner program. Until that is approved, export Orders and Payments from Toast and drop the file in; Steward reads the same sales either way. There is no live connection to read: you drop in its export or statement in Settings, Connections.
